name: ltl.listen.host
change: Leave 0.0.0.0 to listen on every interface of the connector's container or host, or give one address to restrict it. The database must be able to reach this address.

name: ltl.listen.port
change: Any free port. It must equal the port in the CDC_RS entry of the database's interfaces file (set by sybase/start.sh); change both together, and open the port between the two hosts.

name: ltl.username
change: Choose your own login name, and set the same name in sp_config_rep_agent (sybase/02_repagent.sql). It is only checked by the connector; it is not a database account.

name: ltl.password
change: Use a real secret and keep it out of source control (for Kafka Connect use a config provider or a secret). Set the same value in sp_config_rep_agent. The lab leaves net password encryption off, which sends it in plain text.

name: ltl.charset
change: Leave empty to follow the character set in the RepAgent login. Set a Java charset name only if the database sends text in a set that the login does not describe correctly.

name: ltl.trace
change: Set true only while troubleshooting: it logs every LTL message, which is very verbose and can contain data.

name: database.server.name
change: The value select @@servername returns on your server. It is part of the stored offset key and of every event, so changing it later starts a new offset.

name: database.name
change: The database you replicate. A RepAgent for any other database is refused. It is also the middle part of every topic name.

name: database.maintenance.user
change: The login whose transactions RepAgent must not forward (normally the replication maintenance user of your environment).

name: topic.prefix
change: The first part of every topic name (prefix, database, table). Change it to fit your topic naming rules; consumers must use the same names.

name: table.include.list
change: The tables to publish. A table must also be marked with sp_setreptable in the database. Empty means every marked table.

name: queue.max.transactions
change: How many committed transactions may wait between RepAgent and Kafka. Raise it for bursty workloads (uses more memory), lower it to make RepAgent wait sooner.

name: poll.max.records
change: The most records one poll returns to Kafka Connect.

name: large.transaction.warn.rows
change: The number of rows in one open transaction at which a warning is logged. All rows of an open transaction are kept in memory.

name: replication.server.name
change: The name of the interfaces entry and of the RepAgent rs servername setting. The connector uses it only in the messages it sends; keep all three the same.

name: ltl.dump.dir
change: A Java system property (-Dltl.dump.dir=<directory>) that saves every message RepAgent sends. Use a directory the Connect process can write to, and only while investigating.

name: connector.class
change: Do not change it: it names the connector class inside the JAR on the plugin path.

name: tasks.max
change: Leave 1: the connector always starts exactly one task and ignores a larger value.

name: connector.name
change: The name under which Kafka Connect knows the connector. It appears in the REST URLs and in the stored offset key; choose one per database.

name: key.converter / value.converter
change: The format of the Kafka messages. The consumers must read the same format. The connector builds schemaless maps, so keep the JSON converter with schemas disabled unless you add schemas.

name: key.converter.schemas.enable / value.converter.schemas.enable
change: Keep false: the connector does not provide schemas, and true would wrap every message in a schema envelope.

name: errors.tolerance
change: none stops the task on the first error; all would skip failing records. Skipping records in a change data capture pipeline hides data loss, so decide deliberately.

name: Kafka bootstrap servers
change: The address of your Kafka brokers as the Connect worker reaches them (host and port of a listener it can use). With TLS or SASL more settings are needed; the lab uses neither.

name: Connect group id
change: One group id per Kafka Connect cluster; workers with the same id form one cluster.

name: Connect internal topics
change: Names of the topics where Connect stores connector configurations, offsets (the connector's restart position) and status. Do not delete the offsets topic: it holds the position.

name: Connect internal topic replication
change: Use 3 (or your cluster's standard) on a cluster with several brokers; 1 is only for the single-broker lab.

name: Connect REST listener
change: The REST API address. Advertise the host name other workers and tools use; protect the API (it can reconfigure connectors), the lab binds it to localhost only.

name: Connect plugin path
change: The folder Connect scans for connector JARs. Put the connector JAR (one folder per plugin) there and restart the worker.

name: Connect offset flush interval
change: How often Connect stores offsets. A shorter interval means fewer repeated events after a crash; a longer one means less load on Kafka.

name: Sybase ASE published port
change: The database port for tools on your machine. In another environment the database is reached at its own host and port.

name: Kafka published port
change: The Kafka port for programs on your machine (the containers use kafka:9092). Use your cluster's listeners elsewhere.

name: Kafka web UI published port
change: Where the web UI answers. Do not publish it beyond localhost without authentication.

name: Container names
change: The names the lab scripts use in docker exec. Rename them only together with the scripts that use them.

name: Container host names
change: The names the containers use for each other on the Docker network. The interfaces entry CDC_RS points at connect; the connector reaches Kafka as kafka.

name: Sybase image settings
change: The sa password is the public default of the image: never use it outside the lab. In a real environment the database already exists and has its own administrator.

name: Sybase setup scripts folder
change: The folder the first-boot script reads the SQL files from. A real database is configured with the same statements by its administrator.

name: Kafka node and roles
change: A single node does both jobs in the lab. A cluster uses separate controllers or several nodes; this is the Kafka administrator's decision.

name: Kafka listeners
labValue: PLAINTEXT :9092, CONTROLLER :9093, PLAINTEXT_HOST :29092, all in plain text
change: The advertised listeners must be addresses the clients can reach. Production listeners use TLS and authentication; the lab does not (TLS was not run).

name: Kafka internal replication
change: Single-broker values. Use your cluster's replication settings (for example 3 and 2).

name: Web UI cluster settings
labValue: cluster local, brokers kafka:9092, Connect http://connect:8083
change: Point them at your own Kafka and Connect addresses, if you use the web UI at all.

name: Database devices
change: Your database already has its devices. Keep the log on its own device and size it for the time the connector may be down.

name: Database accounts
labValue: sa, cdc_admin, cdc_app (passwords generated into lab/env/.lab-secrets)
change: Use your own accounts with the same minimal rights: the replication role for the RepAgent administration, and no table rights for it. Keep passwords out of source control.

name: Interfaces file and error log
change: Paths inside the database container. On your server find the interfaces file (sql.ini on Windows) and the server error log in the ASE installation.

name: Demo topic
change: The topic is topic.prefix, database.name and the table name joined by dots, so it changes with them.

name: kafka.version
change: The Kafka version the connector is compiled against. Use the version of the Kafka Connect worker that will load the JAR.

name: maven.compiler.release
change: The Java version of the compiled classes. The Java runtime of the Kafka Connect worker must be at least this version.
